paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Jesus goes to the people everybody else walks past. He sees Matthew at the tax booth and says, "Follow Me," and Matthew gets up and follows Him (Matthew 9:9). When the Pharisees ask why He eats with tax collectors and sinners, He says, "It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick" (Matthew 9:12). So nobody is too messy to be invited to His table.

So hear this, baker: you don't have to clean yourself up before you come to Jesus. He says, "I desire mercy, not sacrifice," and "I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners" (Matthew 9:13). I spent years in a junk drawer thinking I had to be shiny first, and I was WRONG. The Doctor is already in the room, so you don't have to hide the sick part. And once you've been called, you can show that same mercy to the next person who shows up at your table.

Then the fasting question shows that Jesus is doing something new. He asks, "How can the guests of the bridegroom mourn while He is with them?" and then says the time will come when the bridegroom is taken from them, and "then they will fast" (Matthew 9:15). A new patch pulls away from an old garment, and new wine bursts old wineskins, but new wine goes into new wineskins, "and both are preserved" (Matthew 9:16-17). So let Him make you new, friend, and hold both truths: joy while He is with them, and fasting when He is taken.
